To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following are important factors for the formation and functioning of groups that are managing common resources: • A high level of social capital, measured in terms of trust, norms, social networks, and participation in formal organizations • The existence of a group that can provide a platform for collective action • The existence of external support • The availability of resources to invest in collective management activities • The existence of an institutional framework that supports collective action • The availability of a local leader with a high social status and who is trusted

(a) social capital is an important resource for sustainable natural resource management; (b) social capital is a multidimensional concept; (c) social capital is not a panacea, but it can contribute to sustainability; (d) social capital can be created, but it is a difficult process; (e) social capital is context specific; (f) social capital is difficult to measure; (g) there is a need for more research to understand the relationship between social capital and sustainable resource
social capital can help to reduce poverty, and that social capital can be created and enhanced through collective action.
